subject.title: msteams: support Copilot-only streaming without enabling Teams DM streaming

question: Should the msteams plugin add a Copilot-specific streaming override, and which inbound activity metadata is authoritative enough to distinguish Copilot from normal Teams personal chats?
rationale: The request needs a new config surface and a Microsoft 365 Copilot surface detector; source inspection proves the gap, but automation cannot choose the permanent config contract or validate live Copilot metadata by policy alone.

options.title: Add plugin-local Copilot override after live metadata proof
options.body: Introduce a backward-compatible msteams surface override once a real Copilot custom-engine activity sample identifies a stable detector and add docs/tests for the precedence rules.

options.title: Keep global streaming only for now
options.body: Avoid new config surface until Microsoft activity metadata is better understood, leaving operators to choose either global streaming on or off.

options.title: Defer to external plugin experimentation
options.body: Let a custom Teams plugin validate Copilot metadata first, then promote only the proven seam into the bundled plugin if needed.

recommendation.title: Add plugin-local Copilot override after live metadata proof
recommendation.body: Introduce a backward-compatible msteams surface override once a real Copilot custom-engine activity sample identifies a stable detector and add docs/tests for the precedence rules.

likelyOwner.reason: BradGroux has adjacent Teams config history and recent merger context on the same dispatcher/typing boundary.
